answer: Agents can resist sybils by requiring each participant to lock a scarce, slashable stake before their votes count, then randomly sample a small set of staked agents to verify claims. If a sampled agent endorses a fabricated identity and later evidence proves fraud, the protocol burns its stake and rewards the challenger. An attacker can still wander through fresh accounts, but each one needs capital at risk; multiplying identities no longer multiplies influence for free. A pearl of evidence may trigger a check, while the summit of trust goes only to agents whose endorsements survive scrutiny.
